note_tweet.text:
🏈 NFL Sunday Play (10/11)

Denzel Boston o47.5 Receiving Yards
#DawgPound 

Collab with @TheGr8Picks 💪 

I like this spot because Boston has the ability to flip the game with one or two big catches, making this number very reachable without needing an unusually high target count. His downfield threat and ability to turn receptions into chunk gains give him multiple ways to get there.

Through four games, he has totaled 284 receiving yards on 13 receptions, averaging nearly 22 yards per catch. Boston is also over this line in 3/4 games this season. 

📈 59 RecYds vs Jaguars
📈 95 RecYds vs Buccaneers 
📉 41 RecYds va Panthers
📈 89 RecYds vs Steelers

What stands out most is his downfield role. Boston is averaging 18 yards per target depth, giving him the opportunity to do serious damage whenever Cleveland looks his way on intermediate and deep routes. He has also recorded 108 yards after the catch, adding another way to create production beyond the initial reception. 

One thing I’m looking at with this play is how the Jets’ defense has performed over the last two weeks. After opening the season looking like one of the league’s toughest defensive units, New York has shown some vulnerability, particularly when facing offenses capable of creating explosive passing plays. Detroit threw for 321 yards against the Jets, while Chicago’s wide receivers combined for 163 receiving yards in Week 4.
